claims.text: The feedstock is a FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy alloy with a particle-size range of 15–45 μm.
Increasing particle velocity during HVAF-i7 deposition will increase deposition efficiency.
Increasing particle velocity during HVAF-i7 deposition will produce a thicker FeCoNiCrAl bond coat than standard HVAF-i7 settings.
The thicker coating produced at increased particle velocity will remain adherent.
A spray-distance range of approximately 300–350 mm is nozzle-specifically optimal for the proposed HVAF-i7 process.
The proposed process can be applied within internal diameters as small as 120 mm.
Increasing particle velocity increases particle kinetic energy.
Greater particle kinetic energy improves particle impact during deposition.
Greater particle kinetic energy improves particle flattening during deposition.
Improved particle impact and flattening increase deposition efficiency.
Improved particle impact and flattening enable formation of a thicker coating.
Improved particle impact and flattening enable formation of a well-adherent coating.
Increasing particle velocity can increase thickness and deposition efficiency while maintaining minimal as-sprayed oxidation.
The intervention will improve adhesion relative to coatings produced at standard HVAF-i7 settings.
The intervention is expected to remain effective during subsequent high-temperature thermal-barrier service.
Departing from the stated spray-distance, geometry, or service conditions may reduce the intervention's effectiveness.
